issues.title: Dashboard text overflow
issues.description:
# Bug: Long Action Descriptions Overlap Adjacent Items

## Description

A UI bug has been identified where lengthy "Action Descriptions" overflow their container bounds and visually overlap the item below them in the list. This text overflow creates a cluttered interface and introduces a risk of users accidentally selecting the wrong action due to overlapping clickable areas.

We need to update the CSS for this component to handle long text gracefully. Depending on the design system, this should be resolved by either allowing the row height to expand dynamically (word-wrap) or by truncating the text with an ellipsis and providing a tooltip on hover.

## User Story

> **As a** RELAY user, **I want** long action descriptions to be formatted correctly without bleeding into other rows, **So that** I can clearly read the descriptions and avoid accidentally clicking the wrong action.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to the view containing the Action Descriptions list.
2. Create or identify an action with an unusually long text description that exceeds the column width.
3. Observe the list view.
4. **Expected Result:** The text should either wrap to a new line (expanding the row height) or truncate gracefully (e.g., "Long description...").
5. **Actual Result:** The text overflows its container and overlaps the text/row directly below it.

## Additional Context

* **Origin:** Customer feedback during testing.
* **Risk/Complexity:** Low. This is a front-end styling issue.
* **Implementation Recommendation:** Apply appropriate CSS (e.g., `word-wrap: break-word;` and `white-space: normal;` for multi-line, or `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;` if single-line truncation is preferred).

---

## Acceptance Criteria (BDD)

```gherkin
Feature: Prevent Text Overlap on Long Action Descriptions
  In order to maintain a clean and usable interface
  As a RELAY user
  I need long text descriptions to be contained within their designated UI boundaries

  Background:
    Given a user is logged into the RELAY system
    And the user is viewing a list containing Action Descriptions

  Scenario: Viewing an action with a very long description
    Given an action exists with a description that exceeds the visual width of its container
    When the user views the action in the list
    Then the text must not overlap the row below it
    And the row height should dynamically expand to accommodate the text OR the text should truncate with an ellipsis
    And the clickable area (hitbox) for the action must not overlap with adjacent actions

  Scenario: Interacting with truncated text (If truncation is chosen as the fix)
    Given an action description is truncated due to length
    When the user hovers their mouse over the truncated description
    Then a tooltip or expanded view should display the full action description
```

issues.title: Bug: Base Contract Detail View Displays Incorrect "Active" Status
issues.description:
# Bug: Base Contract Detail View Displays Incorrect "Active" Status

## Description

A bug has been identified where the Base Contract detail page consistently displays the status as "Active," regardless of the contract's actual status. As shown in the user-provided screenshot, the "Base Contracts Overview" list correctly shows a status like "Close-out," but when a user clicks on that contract, the detail page incorrectly shows "Active." This creates a data discrepancy and can mislead users about the contract's current state.

The correct status values are: "Active", "Dormant", "Close-Out", and "Archived". The detail view must reflect the same status as the overview list.

## User Story

> **As a** RELAY user, **I want** the status on the contract detail page to accurately match the contract's real status, **So that** I can trust the information I see and avoid confusion about whether a contract is active, closed, or archived.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to the "Base Contracts Overview" screen.
2. Find a contract in the list that has a status other than "Active" (e.g., "Close-out").
3. Click on that contract row to navigate to its detail page.
4. **Expected Result:** The detail page should display the same status shown in the overview list (e.g., "Close-out").
5. **Actual Result:** The detail page incorrectly displays the status as "Active."

## Additional Context

* **Origin:** Customer feedback during testing.
* **Risk/Complexity:** Low. This is likely a data-binding issue where the wrong data field is being referenced on the detail page component.

---

## Acceptance Criteria (BDD)

```gherkin
Feature: Accurate Contract Status Display
  In order to trust the data presented in the system
  As a RELAY user
  I need the contract status to be consistent between the overview list and the detail page.

  Background:
    Given a user is logged into the RELAY system
    And a contract exists with a status of "Close-out"
    And the "Base Contracts Overview" list correctly displays this status

  Scenario: Viewing a non-active contract's details
    When the user clicks on the "Close-out" contract to view its detail page
    Then the detail page must display the status as "Close-out"
    And the detail page must NOT display the status as "Active"

  Scenario Outline: Status consistency for all states
    Given a contract exists with a status of "<Status>"
    When the user navigates to that contract's detail page
    Then the detail page must display the status as "<Status>"

    Examples:
      | Status      |
      | Active      |
      | Dormant     |
      | Close-Out   |
      | Archived    |
```

issues.title: Nginx and Tomcat routing for proper URL resolution
issues.description:
**CURRENTLY:** 

* `/relay` - "can't read this page" message in browser, shows https://www.apps.example.com:8080/relay/ in address bar
* `/RELAY` - 404 error, nginx/1.31.2, shows https://www.apps.example.com/RELAY in address bar
* `/relay/` - works, shows https://www.apps.example.com/relay/ in address bar
* `/RELAY/` - works, shows https://www.apps.example.com/relay/ in address bar

---

_the following was generated in chat with an internal AI assistant_

**BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front):** The presence of Nginx in the 404 error confirms this is a dual-layered issue between your proxy and your application server. 
* The **port `8080` leak** happens because Tomcat is issuing a redirect to append a trailing slash, but it doesn't know it sits behind Nginx, so it uses its internal port. 
* The **Nginx 404 error** happens because your current Nginx rules successfully rewrite `/RELAY/` to `/relay/`, but the rule fails to catch the exact string `/RELAY` (without the slash), treating it as a missing file.

---

### Resolution Checklist: Nginx & Tomcat Routing

#### Phase 1: Correct the Nginx Reverse Proxy Configuration
**Objective:** Fix the 404 error for `/RELAY` and ensure Nginx passes the correct external host information to Tomcat so Tomcat stops leaking port 8080.

*   [ ] **1. Locate the Nginx Configuration:** Open the active site configuration file for `www.apps.example.com` (typically found in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/` or `/etc/nginx/sites-available/`).
*   [ ] **2. Add a Case-Insensitive Rewrite Rule:** Above your existing `location` blocks for this app, add a rewrite rule to catch the missing trailing slashes for both upper and lowercase variants. This forces a clean browser redirect to the canonical path:
    ```nginx
    # Catch /relay or /RELAY without a slash and redirect to canonical /relay/
    rewrite ^/(?i)relay$ /relay/ permanent;
    ```
    *(Note: The `(?i)` makes the regex case-insensitive in Nginx).*
*   [ ] **3. Enforce Proxy Headers:** Ensure the primary `location /relay/` block explicitly passes the external Host and protocol headers to Tomcat. 
    ```nginx
    location /relay/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/relay/;
        
        # These headers are critical to stop Tomcat from leaking port 8080
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port 443;
    }
    ```
*   [ ] **4. Validate and Reload Nginx:**
    *   Run `nginx -t` to verify syntax.
    *   Run `systemctl reload nginx` (or equivalent) to apply changes safely without dropping active connections.

#### Phase 2: Configure Tomcat for Proxy Awareness
**Objective:** Tell Tomcat it is operating behind a secure proxy so that any internal redirects it generates use `https://www.apps.example.com` instead of `http://localhost:8080`.

*   [ ] **1. Locate Tomcat's `server.xml`:** Open `<TOMCAT_HOME>/conf/server.xml`.
*   [ ] **2. Update the HTTP Connector:** Find the `<Connector port="8080"...>` block. Add the proxy-awareness attributes (`proxyName`, `proxyPort`, `scheme`, and `secure`). The updated block should look like this:
    ```xml
    <Connector port="8080"
               protocol="HTTP/1.1"
               connectionTimeout="20000"
               redirectPort="443"
               proxyName="www.apps.example.com"
               proxyPort="443"
               scheme="https"
               secure="true" />
    ```
*   [ ] **3. Restart Tomcat:** Restart the Tomcat service to apply the connector changes (e.g., `systemctl restart tomcat`).

#### Phase 3: Verification Testing
**Objective:** Confirm all four URLs now resolve gracefully to the canonical application path. **Important:** Instruct the tester to clear their browser cache or use an Incognito/Private window, as browsers aggressively cache 301/302 redirects.

*   [ ] **Test 1 (`/relay`):** Navigate to `https://www.apps.example.com/relay`
    *   *Expected Result:* URL automatically updates to `https://www.apps.example.com/relay/` and page loads successfully. (Port 8080 is no longer visible).
*   [ ] **Test 2 (`/RELAY`):** Navigate to `https://www.apps.example.com/RELAY`
    *   *Expected Result:* URL automatically updates to `https://www.apps.example.com/relay/` and page loads successfully. (404 error is gone).
*   [ ] **Test 3 (`/relay/`):** Navigate to `https://www.apps.example.com/relay/`
    *   *Expected Result:* Page loads successfully with no extra redirects.
*   [ ] **Test 4 (`/RELAY/`):** Navigate to `https://www.apps.example.com/RELAY/`
    *   *Expected Result:* URL automatically updates to `https://www.apps.example.com/relay/` and page loads successfully.
